subject: Request: temporary SLA throttle and model pin for Model3r p99 step increase
messages:
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Model3r — observed step increase in p99 (short lived but sustained across routes)

Team,

We started seeing a step-like increase in p99 latency for model3r at ~08:44 UTC across Solventa routes (inference route /chat and /summarize). Summary: p99 up ~40% vs baseline over the last 20 minutes, p95 also rose ~12%. CPU/GPU utilization looks normal; KV cache hit rate dropped ~30% on requests >1k tokens.

Prelim correlation: a small fraction of requests with long sequences (~3% of traffic) are now keeping KV slots hot longer, which appears to be amplifying tail behavior in the runtime. This aligns with the model3r-v3 rollout we started at 08:30 UTC.

Immediate mitigations I can execute if we get authorization:
- Apply traffic throttle to Solventa routes (reduce to 60% of normal qps) for a rolling 4-hr window to buy time for analysis.
- Pin traffic for Solventa to model3r-v2.1 (previous stable variant) at the routing layer.
- Enable aggressive prefix caching for the affected customer routes for 2 hours.

Attachments: perf-snapshot-20270403.png (p90/p95/p99 chart), traces-20270403.zip (sample traces and KV cache heatmap).

If you authorize, I will enact throttle + pin immediately and follow up with a post-mortem once we confirm root cause. Please reply with APPROVE/DECLINE and any constraints (credit/notice window) you want in the customer comms.

-David

David Kim
Principal SRE, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Wu <alex.wu@solventa.com>, ops@solventa.com
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 09:32:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Model3r — observed step increase in p99 (short lived but sustained across routes)

Thanks David — good catch.

Proposed path (minimal customer disruption + SLA protection):
1) Authorization requested: temporary traffic throttle to 60% and pin Solventa traffic to model3r-v2.1. Window: initial 4 hours starting on authorization.
2) Customer notice: short note explaining we are applying a temporary traffic limit while we investigate; estimated impact: 3–8% tail reduction for interactive flows, legacy batch unaffected. I will draft the comms (MAP-solventa-draft-v1.pdf attached).
3) Monitoring gates: if p99 does not trend back toward baseline within 90 minutes after throttle/pin, Eng will trigger the rollback playbook and consider a controlled rollback of the v3 rollout for other customers.

Ben / Stephanie — I need an explicit APPROVAL or an alternate instruction. Ben, please advise on allowances for credits if the throttle reduces throughput beyond SLAs.

Priya
Head of Sales (EMEA) — Redwood Inference
(priya_natarajan@redwood.com)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 09:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Model3r — observed step increase in p99 (authorization)

APPROVE for temporary throttle to 60% and pin to model3r-v2.1 for Solventa routes.

Notes/constraints:
- Limit customer-facing credit exposure: we authorize up to a 6% revenue-equivalent credit cap for this action; any additional credit needs finance signoff.
- Customer comms: be explicit about potential degraded tail behavior for long-seq jobs; we should offer a short post-mitigation call if they want a deeper readout.
- If p99 has not meaningfully improved after 90 minutes, David: proceed with the rollback playbook for the v3 rollout (per standard rollback steps) and loop in Legal for any contract implications.

David, please proceed when ready. Stephanie, Priya — I appreciate you looping the customer.

Ben Carter
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@solventa.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, ops@solventa.com
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Model3r — observed step increase in p99 (customer acknowledgement)

Thanks for the rapid flag and proposed mitigations. A couple quick questions:
- Can you confirm expected visible impact to our production users (desktop web chat) if you throttle to 60%? Will we see queued requests or graceful shedding?
- ETA on when the pin/throttle will be live?

We appreciate the transparency; please keep the comms short and concrete. Ops is standing by for a short post-mitigation sync if needed.

—Alex
